children: Super Retail Group's trading update brings little cheer at Macquarie. Sales momentum slowed over the latter part of the September quarter and a note from one of the investment bank's analysts posits that conditions have probably further deteriorated due to higher fuel prices and an expectation of more central-bank interest-rate rises. The analyst highlights the absence of disclosure around October sales, and limited commentary on margins. They think this indicates the Australian retail conglomerate is holding margin rather than aggressively discounting. Macquarie cuts its target price 13% to 13.30 Australian dollars and keeps a neutral rating on the stock, which is down 0.1% at A$12.63. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
